STILLING BASIN FOR ENHANCED FLOOD MANAGEMENT DOWNSTREAM OF AN OGEE SPILLWAY: EXPERIMENTAL AND NUMERICAL STUDY

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Zahraa Hussein Hassoon, Fadhel Abdulabbas Hassan
Print ISSN : 2523-5664
Online ISSN : 2523-5672

Doi: 10.26480/wcm.01.2026.497.504

ABSTRACT

A spillway is a type of hydraulic structure used to release surplus water from reservoirs and prevent flooding of dams. Maintaining dam stability and preventing downstream erosion required energy dissipation of the water flow. The purpose of this study is to assess the hydraulic performance of an ogee spillway due to the effect of various hydraulic and geometric parameters related to the geometry of both the spillway and the new configuration of the stilling basin. A stilling basin with a new geometry of floor blocks was employed. A flume of 0.3 m width, 0.45 m height, and 15 m long was used in several laboratory tests to examine the impact of spillway inclination angles (35°, 45°, and 60°) at various values of discharges. To increase energy dissipation efficiency downstream of the spillway, a stilling basin with V-shape obstacles of different heights (3 cm, 4 cm, and 5 cm) and angles (80°, 90°, and 100°) was also utilized. Additionally, two-phase (water–air) flow was simulated numerically using ANSYS Fluent 18.2 software based on the volume of fluid (VOF) approach and the conventional k–ε turbulence model. The results demonstrated that, in comparison to a standard basin, the use of impediments within the stilling basin significantly increased energy dissipation efficiency. The flow behavior was also clearly affected by the spillway angle and the obstacles’ geometric features. Additionally, the results showed a high degree of accuracy in the regression equations and a good correlation between the percent of energy dissipation and other non-dimensional hydraulic and geometric parameters. Additionally, there was strong agreement between the numerical results and the experimental data. This study highlights the need to employ better stilling basin designs to boost spillway hydraulic performance efficiency and energy dissipation.
